NONE: › at the third highest level of the special levels of achievement in a person's studies at a US college or university. The expression comes from Latin, meaning "with praise".
（拉丁語）以優等成績畢業（美國大學優等學位榮譽中的第三等）

example: Ninety three students graduated cum laude.
九十三名學生以優等成績畢業。
a cum laude qualification
優等畢業證書
See also
magna cum laude

NONE: › used to join two nouns, showing that a person or thing does two things or has two purposes; combined with
（用於連接兩個名詞）兼作，連帶，附有

example: This is my bedroom-cum-study.
這是我睡房兼書房。

NONE: › awkward because of being large, heavy, or not effective
› (a plant with) seeds that smell pleasant and are used as a spice, especially in South Asian and Western Asian cooking
（尤指在南亞和中東用作烹飪調味品的）蒔蘿，土茴香子
› a wide piece of cloth worn round the waist, especially by men, as part of formal or Western Asian clothing
（尤指男子正裝或中東男子用的）寬腰帶

T: › [ T ] to collect a large amount of something over a period of time by gradually adding more
I: › [ I ] to gradually increase by combining with other things over a period of time

example: The system has the ability to cumulate data over a number of years.
這個系統有能力長期收集積累資料。
They have cumulated debts of over $10 million.
他們的債務積累到了超過一千萬美元。
These small delays can cumulate and become a problem.
這些小的延遲累積起來可能成為一個大問題。

NONE: › increasing by one addition after another

example: The cumulative effect of using so many chemicals on the land could be disastrous.
使用大量化學物質經年累月會對土地造成災難性的後果。

NONE: › a large, tall type of cumulus cloud that is often dark and brings heavy rain or a thunderstorm
積雨雲（一種高空濃密的大積雲，帶來大雨或雷暴）
› a type of tall, white cloud with a wide, flat base and rounded shape

nimbus
